grades.quote: Typically, this means first transferring the data from the old cache to the main memory and then transferring it from the main memory to the new cache.
grades.reason: Directly explains that a thread resumed on a different processor loses its cached data, causing cache misses and extra cache-coherence traffic through main memory. This is why processor affinity helps throughput.
Covers instruction and memory ordering and memory barriers. It says nothing about the cache cost of moving a thread between CPUs.
